description: Brali Life OS productivity Deep Run, 2026-09-11. Five evidence passes covered interruption recovery, implementation intentions, progress monitoring, notification blocking, and corrective evidence around deadline/time-management claims. The pass was deduplicated against the three existing same-day research waves. Ready-to-resume planning is the strongest genuinely new protocol candidate; if-then planning and progress monitoring are evidence backbones to merge into existing surfaces; notification blocking extends existing notification research; and self-imposed-deadline claims are blocked because the classic 2002 paper is now retracted and a 2026 replication did not reproduce its main effect.

research_candidates.title: Tasks Interrupted: How Anticipating Time Pressure on Resumption of an Interrupted Task Causes Attention Residue and Low Performance on Interrupting Tasks and How a Ready-to-Resume Plan Mitigates the Effects
research_candidates.review_notes: Across four studies, anticipating a pressured return to unfinished work increased attention residue and reduced performance on the interrupting task; a brief ready-to-resume plan mitigated those effects. This supports a narrow pre-switch resumption note, not a universal productivity gain, fixed note length, or claim that all interruptions can be neutralized.

research_candidates.title: Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals
research_candidates.container_title: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
research_candidates.review_notes: Specific plan making reduced cognitive interference associated with unfinished goals in the reported experiments. This is convergent support for offloading an unfinished task into a concrete resumption plan, not evidence for a particular app or template.

research_candidates.title: The when and how of planning: Meta-analysis of the scope and components of implementation intentions in 642 tests
research_candidates.review_notes: Across 642 independent tests, implementation intentions produced positive cognitive, affective and behavioral effects; effects were larger for contingent if-then formats, when motivation was high, and when plans were rehearsed. Use as evidence for cue-response planning, not as a guaranteed effect size for every productivity task.

research_candidates.title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence
research_candidates.review_notes: Meta-analysis of 138 randomized studies (N=19,951). Interventions that increased monitoring of goal progress improved goal attainment on average (d+=0.40); effects were larger when progress was physically recorded or reported/made public. This supports visible progress tracking, but not one universal cadence, dashboard or streak system.

research_candidates.title: Effects of task interruptions caused by notifications from communication applications on strain and performance
research_candidates.review_notes: One-day field experiment, N=247. Disabling automatic communication notifications reduced notification interruptions; the reduction in interruptions was linked through significant indirect effects to higher self-reported performance and lower irritation. The direct intervention effect on performance was not significant and FoMO/telepressure mattered. Use as support for bounded notification-off focus windows, not an always-off prescription.

research_candidates.title: Replication of Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment
research_candidates.review_notes: The 2026 replication of Study 2 from Ariely and Wertenbroch did not reproduce the original deadline effect: deadline changes had negligible effects on reported performance and survey metrics. This directly challenges treating artificial deadlines as a settled productivity hack.

research_candidates.title: Retraction: Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment
research_candidates.review_notes: The publisher now labels the 2002 Ariely-Wertenbroch paper retracted. Brali should not cite the original paper as positive evidence for deadline design.

research_candidates.title: Does time management work? A meta-analysis
research_candidates.review_notes: Meta-analysis of 158 studies / 53,957 participants found moderate relationships between time management and job performance, academic achievement and wellbeing, with substantial heterogeneity. Much of the evidence is correlational. It supports time-management as a broad construct, not any exact planner format, calendar ratio or time-block recipe.

evidence_decisions.supported_claim: When unfinished work must be interrupted, a short resumption plan can reduce attention residue and protect performance in the studied interruption contexts.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: There is a validated exact three-line template.
It has a known universal productivity percentage.
evidence_decisions.notes: Highest-value genuinely new productivity protocol from this pass. Proposed action: before a forced or deliberate switch from unfinished work, capture where you stopped, the next concrete action, and one critical restart detail.

evidence_decisions.source_title: The when and how of planning: Meta-analysis of implementation intentions in 642 tests
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Cue-response implementation intentions are a well-supported self-regulation mechanism; contingent if-then formats performed better on average in the reviewed literature.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Every if-then sentence guarantees behavior change.
Aggregate effect sizes apply to every productivity task.
evidence_decisions.notes: Merge into existing WOOP/task-initiation surfaces when overlapping rather than creating duplicate content. Keep the executable form explicit: If [observable cue], then I will [specific action].

evidence_decisions.source_title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment?
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Increasing progress monitoring improves goal attainment on average; physically recording or reporting progress was associated with larger effects.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Streaks or public leaderboards are universally beneficial.
evidence_decisions.notes: Evidence backbone for existing tracker/progress surfaces. Prefer one measurable progress variable at a task-appropriate checkpoint over indiscriminate tracking.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Effects of task interruptions caused by notifications from communication applications on strain and performance
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Disabling automatic notifications can reduce notification interruptions; in this field experiment, fewer interruptions mediated better perceived performance and lower irritation.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: All notifications should be off all day for everyone.
The study proves an optimal focus-block duration.
The effect is independent of FoMO and response expectations.
evidence_decisions.notes: Strengthen the existing notification-batching surface rather than create a redundant always-off hack. Protect non-urgent focus windows while preserving explicit urgent-channel and role exceptions.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Replication of Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: The 2026 replication did not reproduce the classic deadline effect, while the publisher now marks the 2002 source retracted.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Artificial deadlines are a settled evidence-based productivity intervention.
Retraction proves that deadlines never matter in any context.
evidence_decisions.notes: Block any new Brali hack whose scientific rationale rests mainly on Ariely & Wertenbroch (2002), and audit any existing deadline guidance for provenance.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Does time management work? A meta-analysis
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Time management has moderate positive relationships with performance and wellbeing at the construct level, with substantial heterogeneity.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: This validates a specific planner, calendar ratio, time-block length or branded method.
evidence_decisions.notes: Wording guardrail: broad time-management evidence cannot be used to invent scientifically optimal implementation details.
